findings.claim: The runtime-settings destination's matchPaths include the broad "/admin" prefix, so `isDestinationActive(runtime-settings, pathname)` returns true for every /admin/* route, causing the desktop rail to mark both the real destination (e.g. Knowledge) and "Runtime settings" as active with duplicate aria-current="page".
findings.evidence: matchPaths: ["/admin", "/admin/runtime", "/admin/approvals", "/admin/protocols", "/admin/settings", ...] combined with `matchesPath` (`pathname === candidate || pathname.startsWith(`${candidate}/`)`) means /admin/knowledge, /admin/agents, /admin/runs, /admin/providers etc. all match. The ordering guard only helps `findDestinationForPath` (first-match wins); `nav-rail.tsx` RailLink calls `isDestinationActive(destination, pathname)` per link, bypassing that guard. Spec violation: spec.md Scenario "Admin-backed work route is active" states "the generic Configure destination MUST NOT claim that route".
findings.suggested_fix: Match "/admin" exactly only (e.g. split matchPaths into exactPaths/prefixPaths, or make isDestinationActive return false when an earlier destination in NAV_DESTINATIONS also matches the pathname). Add a test asserting isDestinationActive(runtimeSettings, "/admin/knowledge") === false and that only one rail link has aria-current on /admin/* work routes.

findings.claim: `event.preventDefault()` is only called inside the gated branch, so Ctrl+K pressed from an editable control or while any dialog is open falls through to the browser default (Chrome/Edge jump to the omnibox/search bar), yanking focus out of the app.
findings.evidence: `if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && event.key.toLowerCase() === "k" && !isEditableTarget(event.target) && !hasOpenDialog()) { event.preventDefault(); ... }` — when isEditableTarget or hasOpenDialog is true, no preventDefault runs. The new test "does not intercept the global shortcut from an editable control" only asserts the palette doesn't open; it doesn't assert the browser default was suppressed.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `event.preventDefault()` unconditionally once the modifier+K chord matches, then gate only the `setCommandPaletteOpen(true)` action on editable-target/dialog checks.

findings.claim: The diff removes the only Cmd/Ctrl+K keydown handler from AdminShell but keeps the `commandOpen` state and `setCommandOpen` setter, so the admin cmdk command palette may now be unreachable via keyboard (and if no other trigger exists, entirely dead) while coexisting with the new global Base UI palette.
findings.evidence: Removed hunk: `useEffect(() => { const onKeyDown = (event) => { if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && event.key.toLowerCase() === "k") { event.preventDefault(); setCommandOpen((open) => !open); } }; document.addEventListener("keydown", onKeyDown); ... }, []);` with `import { type FC, useEffect, useMemo, useState }` reduced to drop useEffect, yet `setCommandOpen(false)` remains in the file. No replacement trigger is added in this diff.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire the admin palette's open state to a visible trigger, or remove the now-orphaned commandOpen state/palette and let the shell's global palette own the shortcut (design.md says the app-wide shell is the authoritative top-level chrome).

findings.claim: The diff silently migrates every assistant-ui primitive (ScrollToBottom, Composer.Send/Cancel, ActionBar.Copy/Edit, BranchPicker) from the `asChild` composition API to Base UI's `render` prop; if the installed @assistant-ui/react version still uses the Radix-style `asChild` API, the send/cancel/copy/branch controls lose their primitive behavior and children render unwrapped, and nothing in the diff's tests exercises this file.
findings.evidence: Hunks like `<ThreadPrimitive.ScrollToBottom render={<TooltipIconButton .../>}>` replacing `<ThreadPrimitive.ScrollToBottom asChild>`, repeated for Composer.Send, Composer.Cancel, ActionBar.Copy, ActionBar.Edit, BranchPicker.Previous/Next. This API migration is outside the stated C-10 scope (shell + brand) and no test or acceptance criterion covers enhanced-thread; the package version cannot be confirmed from the packet.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the installed assistant-ui version supports the `render` prop (post-Base-UI-migration release); if not, revert these hunks and keep only the logo/token changes. Add at least a smoke test rendering EnhancedThread composer controls.

findings.claim: An unconditioned dark favicon link is placed before the media-scoped light/dark links, so browsers that select the first matching icon link will always pick the dark icon and never evaluate the prefers-color-scheme variants, defeating the light/dark favicon selection.
findings.evidence: `<link rel="icon" ... href="/brand/uar-favicon-dark.svg" />` (no media) appears before `<link ... media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)">` and `<link ... media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">`; the unconditioned link matches every color scheme. The new uar-logo.test.ts only asserts the strings are present, not their order or exclusivity.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit only the two media-scoped links (light + dark), or move the unconditioned fallback after them.

findings.claim: The collapsed readiness indicator puts `aria-label` on a plain `<div>` with no role, which ARIA prohibits on generic elements and assistive technologies ignore, so the collapsed rail's readiness status has no accessible name.
findings.evidence: Collapsed branch: `<div className="mx-auto mb-4 ..." aria-label={`${statusText}. ${modeText}${versionText}`} title={...}>` with only an aria-hidden dot inside — no role attribute, so the label is not exposed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `role="img"` (or `role="status"`) to the collapsed container so the aria-label is valid and announced.

findings.claim: The PWA icon set regresses: the sole remaining icon drops the `maskable` purpose, so Android install/adaptive-icon treatment is lost, and the only shipped icon is the dark-variant 512px PNG.
findings.evidence: Replaced `{ src: "/apple-touch-icon.png", sizes: "180x180", purpose: "any maskable" }` with `{ src: "/brand/png/uar-appicon-dark-512.png", sizes: "512x512", purpose: "any" }` — no maskable entry remains anywhere in the manifest.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a second icon entry with `"purpose": "maskable"` backed by a safe-zone-aware asset (e.g. the appicon PNGs with padding), keeping the 512 "any" entry.

findings.claim: The brand-contract test hard-couples the frontend suite to `docs/ui/logo/` and only filters a top-level `.DS_Store`, so a nested metadata file (e.g. `png/.DS_Store`) or any drift in the docs directory breaks the frontend build's tests for reasons unrelated to frontend code.
findings.evidence: `filesBelow(resolve(projectRoot, "../docs/ui/logo")).filter((file) => file !== ".DS_Store")` — the filter matches only the exact top-level name, while `filesBelow` returns slash-joined relative paths, so nested `.DS_Store` entries slip through; `docs/ui/logo` contents are not part of this diff and cannot be verified.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter with `!file.split("/").includes(".DS_Store")` (or basename check) and record the expected asset manifest explicitly in the test rather than deriving it from a mutable docs directory.
